question: A patient presents on Day 5 of continuous fever suspected to be enteric fever. Which investigation offers the HIGHEST diagnostic yield at this stage?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Bone marrow culture has 80–90% sensitivity at any stage of illness and remains positive even after a few doses of antibiotics — it is the gold standard. Blood culture (60–80% in Week 1) is the practical first choice at the bedside.

Incorrect. The Widal test detects serum antibodies which take 7–10 days to rise to diagnostic levels. In Week 1, antibody titres are usually below the diagnostic threshold. Widal is most useful in Week 3 when antibody titres are highest.

Incorrect. Stool culture has its highest yield in Weeks 3–4 when organisms are shed from the gallbladder into the intestine. In the first week, the organism is primarily in the blood and reticuloendothelial system, not yet in stool in significant numbers.

Incorrect. Urinary excretion of Salmonella Typhi occurs from Week 3 onwards, and urine culture has lower sensitivity than both blood and stool cultures. It is not the investigation of choice in any week.

overallFeedback.feedback: Match the test to the pathogenesis timeline: organisms appear in the blood first (Week 1), antibodies rise later (Weeks 2–3), and stool/urine excretion occurs last (Weeks 3–4). Bone marrow culture has 80–90% sensitivity at any stage.

The week-wise approach: Week 1 → blood culture (practical) / bone marrow culture (gold standard); Week 2 → blood culture + Widal; Week 3 → Widal (peak antibodies) + stool culture; Week 4+ → stool and urine culture. Bone marrow culture works at any stage.
